dossier.public_summary: The 12-day dip looks planet-sized at 1.54 R_earth but its depth changes by nearly 300% between sectors and between individual transits, with three out of ten transits much deeper than the rest. A secondary dip at 42% depth and a duration much longer than expected for this small M dwarf point to a stellar eclipse or blend, not a planet on the target.

reasons.why: Depth is not stable; SPOC 2-min gives 514 ppm, 3726 ppm, 128 ppm in three sectors despite same pipeline. A planet on target should have one depth. This is a light-curve systematics / blend, not a calibration offset.
reasons.value: changes_within_a_source, p_constant=1.62e-17, depth_change_pct=289, QLP err 168, SPOC err 170, sector 35 3726 err 350

reasons.why: Ten transits are wildly inconsistent with each other and one sector carries almost the whole signal. A real planet requires consistent transits.
reasons.value: p_consistent=9.498100825030369e-35, chi2=183.48 dof=9, share_of_top_3=0.954, outlier epoch 61 3817 ppm sigma 7.2

reasons.why: A secondary at ~0.35 phase with S/N just above a brightening bump and ~42% of the primary depth is typical for a stellar eclipsing binary at this period, and supports secondary over noise.

Transit is much longer than central for this 0.3899 Rsun M dwarf and the light-curve density is inconsistent with the stellar density, favouring a longer stellar eclipse / off-target blend over a small planet.
reasons.value: duration ratio=1.563, observed_h=3.497 central_h=2.238, star_density_penalty=85.36, fit_b=0.4906

reasons.why: Star is a fast, large-amplitude rotator (909-11338 ppm) and the signal period is ~1.18x the 10.14-d rotation, with large phase-curve swing, often seen when systematics from spots mimic a dip or when a blended binary mimics the signal. Low planet_rank 0.05 matches blend/false-alarm population.
